title: SDLC Task Envelope v1
description: The shared envelope for one actionable SDLC task record. The envelope owns processing state and the common task wrapper; the wrapper owns task workflow status, the canonical taskSchema selector, and the two-root intent/result payload boundary. The host must validate intent and result against the selected task contract and its root-specific schemas.
$comment: JSON Schema validates the envelope fields and the common task wrapper shape. Host-level validation must resolve taskSchema first, validate the corresponding intent and result objects, verify that intentSchema and resultSchema resolve under taskSchema, verify repository-relative references, confirm required references are readable, and enforce that taskType and the selected schemas identify the intended task contract. processingStatus describes whether this envelope has been processed by the host; task.status describes the task workflow and must not be inferred from processingStatus.

schema.description: The versioned envelope contract identifier. It identifies the shared wrapper and must not be used as the task-specific payload schema.

workItemId.description: Stable identity of the parent local or externally originated work item.

taskUid.description: Stable identity of this task, composed from the work-item identity and its eight-digit order key.

orderKey.description: The fixed-width eight-digit position of this task in the work-item tree. Parentage and phase semantics are interpreted by the applicable SDLC tree profile.

parentTaskUid.description: Stable identity of the immediate parent task. The root task has null; every non-root task identifies its structural parent.

taskType.description: The task-kind vocabulary value used to select and describe the concrete task payload. Task kinds are not restricted by parent or child kind; recursive decomposition remains available to every kind.

processingStatus.description: Host processing state for this envelope. unprocessed means processing has not started; processing_in_progress means the host is processing it; processing_completed means this processing pass completed and must not be repeated for the same envelope; processing_blocked or processing_failed records a terminal processing outcome. This state is distinct from task.status and task.result.status.

title.description: Short human-readable title for the bounded task action.

objective.description: The outcome this task is intended to produce. Essential context should be referenced rather than duplicated when it is maintained by another authoritative task or document.
examples: Define the architecture and data flow required for the messaging component.

references.description: Repository-relative context references divided into required inputs and informational context.

dependsOn.description: Task identities whose required results must be available before this task is eligible to execute. An empty array means no declared task dependency.

governance.description: Optional versioned governance contract for governed execution. Its absence is distinct from malformed governance and is reported by the host as missing governance; read-only discovery may still load the envelope.

examples.commitSubject: WI-0006: 02: feat(sdlc): define canonical task governance

task.description: The task workflow wrapper. status is the task's workflow/lifecycle state; taskSchema is the canonical selector for the complete task contract; intent and result are the only task payload roots; intentSchema and resultSchema identify the corresponding subschemas. This wrapper is not the same as the envelope processing state.

status.description: Current workflow state of the task action. The selected task contract may add more specific result statuses, decisions, evidence, review, rework, or delivery states inside result; this status is the host-controlled task lifecycle and is not envelope processing state.

taskSchema.description: Canonical absolute URI identifying the complete task-specific contract. The host resolves this selector in its local schema registry and verifies that its task type agrees with the envelope taskType.

intentSchema.description: Absolute URI reference for the task intent subschema. It must resolve under taskSchema, match taskType, and identify the selected task contract's intent property.

resultSchema.description: Absolute URI reference for the task result subschema. It must resolve under taskSchema, match taskType, and identify the selected task contract's result property.

intent.description: The prospective task boundary, validated against intentSchema.

result.description: The observed task output, validated against resultSchema when the task lifecycle status requires a result. Transitional statuses may omit, null, or partially populate this value; a result does not directly mutate the envelope or work-item lifecycle.

TaskGovernance.description: The versioned, task-owned contract for bounded paths, one exact commit subject, required commit-body sections, and structured local validation procedures. It contains no provider or shell execution semantics.

schema.description: Stable identifier for the governance contract version.

ownedPaths.description: Non-empty set of unique repository-relative files or directory prefixes that the task may change.

commitSubject.description: Exact subject that the single task commit must use; hosts must compare it literally rather than infer or normalize it.
examples: WI-0006: 02: feat(sdlc): define canonical task governance

commitBody.description: Structured declaration of the commit-body sections required by the task.

requiredSections.description: Unique, human-readable section names that must appear in the commit body.

validationProcedures.description: Structured local validation procedure descriptors. These declarations are data only; this schema does not execute commands or permit arbitrary shell strings.

requiredForExecution.description: Whether governed write-capable execution must reject an envelope when this governance block is absent; read-only discovery remains able to report absence.

examples.commitSubject: WI-0006: 02: feat(sdlc): define canonical task governance

ValidationProcedure.description: A bounded local procedure descriptor with an executable identity and argument vector; it is not a shell command string.

id.description: Stable task-local identifier for the procedure.

executable.description: Local executable name or repository-approved tool identity without shell operators, interpolation, or a command line.

arguments.description: Ordered literal argument values passed without shell interpretation.

expectedExitCode.description: Expected numeric process exit code for a successful local procedure.

WorkItemId.description: A work-item identity with an uppercase alphabetic prefix, one hyphen, and a numeric portion. Descriptive suffixes and additional hyphens are not part of the identifier.

TaskUid.description: A task identity composed of a work-item identity, a separator, and an eight-digit order key.

RepositoryPath.description: A non-empty repository-relative path that does not escape the repository through an absolute path or parent traversal.

References.description: The task context boundary. Required references contain information necessary to understand or correctly execute the task; informational references provide useful context without automatically blocking execution when absent.

required.description: Repository-relative paths that must be available and readable before the task can execute. These references may contain essential context that the task objective does not repeat.

informational.description: Repository-relative paths that should be supplied when available but whose absence does not automatically block execution.
